newsitem.title: USA: Sara Lee up on Q3 profit quality -analysts.
newsitem.headline: Sara Lee up on Q3 profit quality -analysts.

text.p: Sara Lee Corp shares rose 1-3/8 to 42 on good quality earnings for the third quarter ended March 29 that met expectations, analysts said.
"The results were right in line, as they always are," Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez said. "The quality of the earnings is really what counts for Sara Lee."

Ghez said Sara Lee's overall unit volume rose four percent, which she called a "very good" increase. Earnings improved despite higher corporate expenses and no reduction in net interest expense, analysts added.
Sara Lee said it expects record results for fiscal 1997.
For the third quarter, Sara Lee reported net earnings of 41 cents per share compared with 37 cents a year earlier.
Schroder Wertheim analyst Robert Cummins said Sara Lee's third quarter results were hurt by foreign currency issues, given the stronger U.S. dollar.

If foreign exchange rates in the third quarter were comparable with a year ago, sales would have been three percentage points higher, Cummins said. Sara Lee's quarterly sales rose 4.6 percent to $4.6 billion.
Cummins added that the effect of foreign currency rates remains a concern for fiscal 1998, although the company continues to expect a double-digit percentage increase in earnings for next year.
